english.title: UK firm exercise European Economic Area right to provide services within one month of receiving a notice
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a UK firm which was not an authorised person, exercised an EEA right to provide services, derived from paragraph 20(3B) of Schedule 3 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, and provided those services within one month of the date on which it received the notice under paragraph 20(3B)(b) of that Schedule
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 21(1)(b) and (2) of Schedule 3 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Paragraph 21(3) of Schedule 3 to the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that in proceedings for an offence under this paragraph, it is a defence for the firm to show that it took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.
(ii) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the 'appropriate regulator' (either the Financial Conduct or the Prudential Regulation Authority) or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
